title: Patterned Photostimulation with Digital Micromirror Devices to Investigate Dendritic Integration Across Branch Points
protocol: Use a high-power laser for photolysis experiments.
Launch the laser output into a multimode fiber for positioning and orientation.
Wind the optical fiber around a piezoelectric fiber stretcher oscillating at ~40 kHz.
Collimate the fiber output with a UV microscope objective (Olympus DApo20UV).
Co-register individual DMD mirrors with specific pixels of the imaging CCD camera.
Use in-house software GUI to assign DMD mirrors corresponding to regions tagged by the mouse on the CCD image.
Tag locations for photo stimulation by moving the cursor over the displayed image and clicking on the region of interest.
Store pattern marked on the computer screen as a series of separate images.
Program timing of laser pulses for each spatial pattern into integrated software with data acquisition program (pClamp).
Initiate data acquisition program to coordinate timing of DMD electronics, gating of the laser, and electrical signal acquisition from the target neuron.
